A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Simple Policy Optimization and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their substantial methodological and experimental differences can be reliably compared.

before.justification: v5 reports original Atari and MuJoCo experiments, including algorithm comparisons, network-depth tests, over-optimization, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v7 reports original benchmark comparisons, network-scaling experiments, and synthetic objective-optimization results in Section 6 and Appendices A and C.

M1.justification: v5's objective multiplies the surrogate objective by a sign-dependent factor involving clipped KL divergence. v7 replaces this with rA - |A|(r-1)^2/(2epsilon). This removes explicit KL-divergence calculation, the dmax parameter, and the special initial-update branch from Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: The Atari and six MuJoCo benchmark tasks remain the main coverage. However, v5 Figure 7's 35 Atari games become 40 in v7 Figure 10: nine games are added, while Enduro, Freeway, Kangaroo, and Krull disappear. v7 also introduces a synthetic Gaussian-advantage test setting.

E2.justification: v7's MuJoCo comparison adds PPO-Penalty, SPU, PPO-RB, TR-PPO, TR-PPO-RB, and RPO alongside PPO-Clip, as verified in Figure 4. Conversely, PPO-Penalty and PPO-EarlyStop disappear from the Atari comparisons, which previously included them in v5 Figures 2 and 10.

E3.justification: The hyperparameter tables change Atari update epochs from 8 to 4 and the reported value-loss coefficient from 1 to 0.5. MuJoCo training changes from task-dependent 3M/10M budgets to 10M steps. v7 introduces deeper policy and ResNet configurations, minibatch-size comparisons, and PPO-normalized final-1% aggregate evaluation; its separate scaling table retains final-10% returns.

E4.justification: v5's KL-threshold sensitivity study and 1,000-epoch game-based over-optimization tests disappear. v7 adds synthetic comparisons of PPO, SPO, and a simple alternative objective, and substantially revises scaling analyses through MuJoCo policy-depth/minibatch tests and Atari ResNet experiments.

E5.justification: v5 reports standard deviations across three Atari seeds and five MuJoCo seeds. v7 retains these practices for training curves but adds a ten-seed MuJoCo comparator evaluation and stratified-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, including aggregate intervals in Figures 4 and 9. This introduces a substantial new uncertainty-reporting framework.

E6.justification: v5's threshold-specific MuJoCo returns and full-training averages are replaced by depth-specific returns and ratio deviations. For example, v7 Table 1 newly reports seven-layer Humanoid returns of 4769.9 for SPO and 614.1 for PPO. Aggregate baseline, ResNet, and synthetic results are also added. These are results under revised methods and settings, not controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v7 introduces TV/KL solution-space inclusion, an optimized-lower-bound comparison, and the epsilon-aligned objective definition and theorem with proofs in Sections 4–5. These substantially replace v5's KL-clipping derivation and theoretical framing; v5's Gaussian KL-divergence proof in Appendix B.6 is removed.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from KL-divergence clipping with low KL and higher policy entropy to a probability-ratio objective supported by TV-based theoretical claims. v7 additionally claims to combine TRPO's guarantees with PPO's efficiency and, in Figure 1, claims the first model-free end-to-end training of extremely deep networks.

C2.justification: v5's explanations connecting low KL divergence to entropy and exploration are replaced by corrective-gradient and TV-trust-region explanations. v7 also interprets the alternative-objective experiment through its use of advantage magnitudes. v5's discussion distinguishing stronger final MuJoCo performance from weaker full-training averages is no longer present.

D1.justification: v7 adds Gymnasium identification, ResNet-18 batch-normalization removal, and more explicit return, value-loss, and entropy calculations. It removes v5's code-availability statement/link, explicit Atari preprocessing description, and detailed CNN architecture diagram. This substantially changes reproducibility documentation; the PDFs do not establish that the external repository itself was withdrawn.

R1.justification: v7 substantially repositions the work around TV-based trust regions, corrective gradients, and deep-network training, with new references including Achiam et al. (2017), Agarwal et al. (2021), Bjorck et al. (2021), and Gan et al. (2024). Several earlier clipping/phasic-policy references and the RLHF/DPO discussion and citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, methodology, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v7 adds dedicated Related Work and Theoretical Results sections, shifts the main experimental emphasis toward MuJoCo, reorganizes the appendices, and removes v5's unfinished checklist.

P2.justification: v7 adopts a two-column layout and adds objective-comparison diagrams, a gradient schematic, aggregate confidence-interval panels, and new scaling displays. It removes extensive KL/entropy/sensitivity panels, restructures the MuJoCo results table, and consolidates the hyperparameter tables. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v7 strengthens empirical support through broader MuJoCo comparisons, bootstrap confidence intervals, and deeper-network experiments. However, it removes reproducibility disclosures and introduces a theoretical inconsistency: Definition 5.1 and Theorem 5.2 require/assert convexity although Equation 18 defines a concave quadratic objective. These empirical gains and unresolved theoretical and reproducibility weaknesses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
